retiredFleetSkills.name: repocontext
retiredFleetSkills.reason: The skill's entire contract is 'exactly eight read-only, job-oriented tools' served by an MCP server named repocontext. No such server exists anywhere on the fleet, so the skill names tools that cannot be called.
retiredFleetSkills.evidence: registry/mcps.json declares twelve servers and repocontext is not among them. All 17 readable host MCP configs were enumerated and none registers it -- codex's config mentions the string only in a stale [projects.'c:\repos\shmindmaster\repocontext'] trust entry, which is a project-trust row, not a server. Both routes the skill documents are dead: the local stdio route runs `pnpm --dir C:/Repos/shmindmaster/repocontext mcp:serve` and that directory does not exist (C:/Repos/shmindmaster holds 18 repos, none named repocontext), and the remote route needs a REPOCONTEXT_MCP_TOKEN no host holds. Deployed to 14 hosts at retirement.
retiredFleetSkills.whyFleetScoped: repowise supersedes it but maps to 8 hosts, only 5 of which overlap the 14 carrying repocontext. A capability-scoped retirement would have cleaned 5, left 9, and reported success.
retiredFleetSkills.corroboratingResidue: A whole-disk sweep (not just the skills directories) also found ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp/repocontext and ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/mcp/repocontext. These are antigravity's own tool-description caches, holding exactly the eight tools the skill documents -- repo.compare, repo.inspect, repo.read, repo.search, wiki.analyze, wiki.catalog, wiki.get, wiki.search -- each with parameters: null. They are stale caches from when repocontext WAS registered, and antigravity's live mcp_config.json does not list it, so they corroborate the retirement rather than contradicting it. Deliberately NOT swept: they are a host's internal cache, not a managed skill, and are the host's to regenerate.

Thin wrapper over AssemblyAI: one routing skill and the two hosted MCP servers (registry/mcps.json#assemblyai, #assemblyai-docs). Installed and enabled per host; hosted usage needs sign-in and is billed. It wraps instead of copies because AssemblyAI/assemblyai-skill has no licence. Media work routes through media-studio, where AssemblyAI runs only when a job names it.

Brave Search API through one skill and a dependency-free Node client (skills/search/scripts/brave.mjs); no MCP server, so nothing runs until a search is made. The key comes from BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY or BRAVE_API_KEY in the environment and is never written to a file. Adapted from the MIT-licensed brave/brave-search-skills; see NOTICE. Search is billed per query by Brave.

Daytona cloud sandboxes through one skill, with no MCP server or hook, so nothing runs until a sandbox is needed. Copied from Apache-2.0 daytona/skills with all SDK reference directories bundled; see NOTICE. Defaults to DAYTONA_API_KEY; explicit DAYTONA_API_KEY1 selection is scoped to the child process, with no automatic account failover. Claude, Factory, Devin and Grok use the vendor plugin from their own catalog; registry/native-connectors.json records those channels.

One skill routes tasks to a native browser that can reach the intended profile, Tencent BrowserSkill for a connected local Chrome or Edge profile, or the bundled agent-browser wrapper for isolated testing and capture. BrowserSkill uses a separately installed bsk CLI and user-enabled extension, with explicit browser and session selection. No MCP server or hooks.
capabilities.hostMappingsNote: Deploy the same routing skill on local agent hosts, including those with native browser tools. OpenCode and Warp consume the skill through scripts/Install-WarpSkills.ps1. Qoder requires an available local client, and Gemini requires an enabled dispatch route and account access before rollout there. BrowserSkill requires access to the desktop user's local daemon and selected browser profile.
